title: GAX-P02 - External transport adapters and upstream revision freeze
outcome: Add fail-closed external baseline transports that preserve the GAXBench metric, provenance, and no-label-leakage contracts while freezing public upstream source revisions and licenses.
rationale: The paper needs external baselines, but importing every heavy model runtime into GAX would make comparison mechanics platform-specific and difficult to reproduce. A shared TypeSafe HTTP transport plus a shell-free JSON command boundary lets open baselines run in their native environments while GAX retains identical item rendering, failure accounting, metrics, and evidence packets.
scope_in: TypeSafe-compatible POST /v1/systemone transport for CLM, Laya, and decider class baselines
Shell-free JSON command transport for external baselines without the shared HTTP protocol
Model-visible rendering that excludes gold labels and evidence relation annotations
Declared transport-only normalization for four-decimal probability serialization
Environment-variable secret reference without secret values in CLI evidence
Exact public source revision and Apache-2.0 license freeze for CLM, Laya, decider, and open-alternative-jev
Offline deterministic transport tests and CLI evidence-packet integration
scope_out: No real external model benchmark result
No claim that adapter-qualified means model-qualified
No GAX model implementation or training
No headline performance or safety claim
acceptance: External model rendering never exposes gold fields or evidence.relation annotations
TypeSafe HTTP requests use one Choice question with exactly the caller-provided action IDs and descriptions
HTTP adapter requires exact action-key equality and rejects malformed or materially unnormalized distributions
Only rounding error explainable by four-decimal per-action serialization may be renormalized, and the correction is recorded in prediction metadata
HTTP API credentials are read by environment-variable name so secret values do not enter evidence-packet command lines
JSON command adapter executes argv without a shell, enforces timeout and output bounds, and surfaces non-zero exits
CLM source is frozen at 7956937c58ed5839c06ddc4dc6b6b61c3a3e4094 with Apache-2.0 source license
Laya source is frozen at 3c68ca2ccf6a83640ab80c20379503fe72c772fd with Apache-2.0 source license
decider source is frozen at 5f91c011f05fa4b685f0845281a0805a56eb0169 with Apache-2.0 source license
open-alternative-jev source is frozen at 4a85df1831b537343c9e133b5150fa3a3b1ce98e with Apache-2.0 source license
Registry distinguishes adapter-qualified from real-model qualification and retains explicit pending reasons
Exact-head CI runs Ruff, mypy strict, pytest, and compileall on Python 3.11/3.12 across Linux and Windows
SG-000004 introduces no external benchmark result, GAX training, PHI, or clinical-performance claim

risk.recovery: Revert SG-000004 and return to canonical P02 core harness at d04460636515c72b4e095f25683ce59df8174ef4. No model weights, clinical datasets, or GAX training artifacts are affected.

minimality.rationale: Three required baselines expose the same TypeSafe System-One HTTP protocol. One rigorously tested transport is smaller and fairer than three bespoke clients; a shell-free command boundary covers non-HTTP runtimes without importing heavy model dependencies.

requirements: Never expose gold labels, sufficiency labels, or evidence relation annotations to an external model.
Never place API-key values in CLI arguments or evidence packets.
Never equate transport qualification with real-model benchmark qualification.
Any probability transport correction must be bounded, deterministic, and explicitly recorded.

unresolved_decisions: Immutable Hugging Face model/tokenizer revisions are frozen only at each real-model qualification run.
The final clinical encoder and structured-output LLM model choices remain unresolved.
Jev remains blocked unless reproducible evaluation access and terms permit matched measurement.
